body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**

UBR7

* **Description of issue**

I don't find any evidence for chromatin remodelling across this orthologous group.
Can you provide evidence for this?
title: GO:0006338	 chromatin remodeling IEA with ARBA00027994

author: ValWood
ValWood
body:
However, the chomatin remodelling annotations do seem to be a little problematic

For these
PomBase	SPBC1347.02	ani1	involved_in	GO:0006338	GO_REF:0000117	IEA	ARBA:ARBA00027994	P	nucleophosmin-like histone chaperone/CENP-A amino terminus domain (NTD) isomerase Ani1/Fkbp39	fkbp39	protein	taxon:4896	20250428	UniProt		
PomBase	SPBC4.05	mlo2	involved_in	GO:0006338	GO_REF:0000117	IEA	ARBA:ARBA00027994	P	ubiquitin protein ligase E3 component human N-recognin 7 homolog Mlo2		protein	taxon:4896	20250428	UniProt		
PomBase	SPCC126.07c	asr1	involved_in	GO:0006338	GO_REF:0000117	IEA	ARBA:ARBA00027994	P	ubiquitin-protein ligase E3 Asr1	pbr1	protein	taxon:4896	20250428	UniProt		
PomBase	SPCC645.13	bye1	involved_in	GO:0006338	GO_REF:0000117	IEA	ARBA:ARBA00027994	P	transcription elongation regulator, PHD finger Bye1		protein	taxon:4896	20250428	UniProt	

Not all histone modification is "chromatin remodelling"

some of these do not appear to be remodelling - In GO assembly, and remodelling are disjoint and  at least some of these appear to be "assembly"

For instance ani1 is involved in CENP-A containing chromatin assembly. This occurs in S-phase and isn't considered to be "remodelling"

@pgaudet  do you agree?
